relations.evidence: The transaction can only be committed if the transactional [durability](../../../server/current/learn/data/durability.md) requirements can be met. The transaction durability level is set by the request-level [durability_level](../n1ql-manage/query-settings.md#durability%5Flevel) parameter.

notable_absence.finding: Like BEGIN TRANSACTION, COMMIT TRANSACTION has no Capella-specific access-control gate at all. Its only prerequisite is durability-capability, not identity/role/credential-type - reinforcing that the transaction-statement family sits entirely outside the access-control model that governs DDL statements in this round.

cross_component_finding: This page links directly to server/'s durability concept page ('../../../server/current/learn/data/durability.md') for an explanation of transactional durability, and cites a numeric server error code ('a 161 error code is generated') without any Capella-specific framing - both consistent with this statement family being shared server/ source content, though not a literal 'Couchbase Server X.Y' version string so not logged against the existing docs-issue.
cross_product_finding: Open question (per task brief): no textual evidence on this page connects COMMIT TRANSACTION to the Java SDK's distributed-transaction feature (sdk:distributed-transaction) or to sdk:transaction-durability. The durability_level parameter here and the SDK's TransactionsConfig.durabilityLevel() setting (see java-sdk/howtos/distributed-acid-transactions-from-the-sdk.json) share the same underlying durability-level enum concept, but this page gives no explicit cross-reference to the SDK feature - flagging the likely-shared-mechanism-but-unconfirmed-by-text situation rather than asserting a relation.
